subject: Follow-up: MedWare privacy requirements & retention approach
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Holt <claire.holt@medware.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — data handling priorities

Hi Claire — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of the items we heard and proposed next steps so your security & legal teams can review: 

1) Scope of PII: You confirmed that patient identifiers (name, DOB, MRN) and full-text clinical notes are considered high-sensitivity and should not be retained in raw form. 
2) Residency: Production inference must run in our EU region (Frankfurt) and customer data should not leave EU-hosted inference.
3) Retention ask: MedWare legal requested an option for either (a) 0-retention for identified PII fields, or (b) a 7-day ephemeral log window for telemetry with immediate redaction of PII.
4) Audit evidence: You asked for SOC2 artifact mapping and a short sample of the request/response log format (sanitized).

Attached: the security questionnaire you sent (we annotated a few answers inline) and a proposed short-retain matrix that maps data classes to suggested retention behavior.

Next steps (mutual action plan):
- Redwood: Draft a pilot SOW for a 6-week technical pilot that implements the 7-day short retention on telemetry + field-level redaction for PII. (Deliverable: redaction-pilot-sow-v1.docx) — target: Nov 23.
- MedWare: Share the list of exact fields that must be zero-retained (if you choose 0-retention) and confirm primary Infosec contact for the questionnaire.
- Both: Schedule a 30-min legal + infosec sync the week of Nov 23.

If MedWare truly needs 0-retention for specific fields, we can evaluate a scoped exception for the pilot (technical and contractual). For production, that will typically require an addendum since it changes operational audit paths — happy to route to our sales-legal team.

Short ask: can you confirm whether you prefer the pilot to be 0-retain for fields or 7-day short-retain with redaction? That decision will determine the SOW language.

Thanks,
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Claire Holt <claire.holt@medware.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — data handling priorities

Rachel — appreciate the thorough recap. Quick clarifications from our side after we looped in security: 

- Preference: Our legal team prefers 0-retention for direct patient identifiers and any free-text clinical notes containing PHI. Telemetry (latency, model ID, non-identifying token counts) can be short-retained (<=7 days).
- Residency: Confirmed — EU-only for inference and logs containing identifiers.
- Audit: We need an audit trail that proves PII fields were redacted before any logs left the inference host. A signed attestation or an automated log hash chain is acceptable.

We can send a redlined version of the questionnaire by end of day tomorrow. If Redwood can propose a technical pilot that demonstrates field-level redaction with a 7-day telemetry window and an optional 0-retain toggle for the PII fields, that would be ideal.

Claire Holt
VP, Product & Security
MedWare.ai
security@medware.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap — pilot framing and legal implications

FYI — forwarding Claire's reply. Ben, can you weigh in on feasibility and whether we can offer a contract addendum path for per-field 0-retention? My quick take:

- Tech: Runtime can apply deterministic field redaction before any request/response are written to logs. We can implement an inline filter that strips configured keys and returns a tokenized placeholder to the model call. That satisfies the 0-retain operational requirement for those fields (no raw PII leaves the inference host).
- Residencies: We can pin the inference to eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) and ensure logging S3/Blob storage is in the same region.
- Evidence: We can produce a signed artifact showing redaction events (hash + timestamp) but legal will push on whether our retention controls are auditable by a third party.

Proposed commercial path:
- Pilot: 6-week pilot with engineering support and one production-like integration (no historical data). Redwood bears pilot work in exchange for a short-term evaluation credit.
- If MedWare requests per-field contractual 0-retention in production: require an Enterprise addendum + 6–8 week security review + operational runbook.

Ben — can you draft the minimal SOW language and the short-retain matrix update? I'll prep a one-page exec note for legal to fast-track review.

-Marissa
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

2) Security questionnaire (MedWare) — Claire to share redlines by Fri Nov 20 (we received them and are reviewing).
3) Legal & Infosec sync — Tue, Nov 24, 09:00 CET (invite sent).
4) Evidence pack — Redwood to produce SOC2 mapping and a sanitized sample of automated redaction logs (sha256 hashes + timestamps) for MedWare review. Target: Nov 26.

Attachments included here are the files we discussed (same as sent earlier). I also added a simple decision table in the proposed-short-retain-matrix.xlsx that maps data class -> recommended default, pilot option, production addendum trigger.

If you confirm now that the pilot should be scoped as: "7-day telemetry window + enforced field-level redaction for identified PII (with contractual 0-retain toggle for those fields)" we'll finalize the SOW accordingly.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.
Rachel
